about: How loud a sound is heard at a time: its volume, or its volume Keyframes (in seconds from its start, each approached by its `ease`, Linear when none) sampled there, times its linear fades; silent before its `start` and after its `end` (seconds into the Clip). Its `fade_in` and `fade_out` (none when absent) are as set: when together they are longer than the sound, both are shortened by the same share to fit. A sound whose `item` is "segment" is a Segment's, from its start on the Timeline (a Transition's overlap included) to its end, its fades fitted to that length; any other, a Music Clip's. A `muted` one (docs/adr/0016) is silent throughout, whatever its volume, Keyframes and fades. A ducked one (a Music Clip's `duck`, in dB, docs/adr/0016) is multiplied by its duck too: 1 away from its `speech` spans (seconds into the Clip), the depth's gain over one, and straight lines between over the `ducking` lead before one and its release after it; where spans' ducks overlap, the lower wins. A `source` one is the Source's sound (a Source Segment, or a Music Clip of the Source), its volume or Keyframes times the Clip's own volume, `source_volume`. A Segment's `tail` is the last seconds of it that the Transition into the next overlaps (its `end` includes them, and its fades are fitted to all of it): the Timeline draws it to where that Transition starts, heard on under it. With `crossfade`, the gains are also those of that Transition taking it away: falling in a straight line from 1 to 0 over its `tail`, as the render's acrossfade does. Each of `at` is [seconds into the Clip, the gain heard there]. Read by backend/tests/test_gain.py and frontend/src/pages/job/editor/loudness.test.ts, so that the render's gain and the preview's can't drift.
